les: Wat elektrisiteit kos, en waar dit onveilig word
kaps_punt: elektrisiteit is duur omdat: dit infrastruktuur vereis, insluitende steenkoolmyne, vervoer, kragstasies, kabels, substasies, bedrading; sommige elektriese toestelle vereis meer elektrisiteit as ander (verhittings toestelle gebruik die meeste); hoe meer elektrisiteit ons gebruik, hoe meer betaal ons en hoe meer steenkool word gebruik; ons kan energie bespaar op baie maniere, insluitend die gebruik van energiebesparende gloeilampe en sonkrag waterverwarmers; onwettige elektriese verbindings is 'n gevaar vir mense, want hulle is dikwels onveilig

items.bewering: Dit begin by steenkoolmyne, waar werkers steenkool uit die grond haal. Treine, trokke of lang vervoerbande bring die steenkool na die kragstasies.

items.bron: US DOE (energy.gov) lighting fact sheet: incandescent bulbs turn ~90% of their energy into heat; CFLs give the same light with 75% less energy and 75% less heat; LEDs use at least 75% (up to 90%) less energy. https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/ES-EE Lighting_080921.pdf

'Minder te doen' is correctly not 'niks'. https://www.kwikot.com/kwiktok-series/episode-6/solar-water-heaters ; https://phys.org/news/2011-06-solar-heaters-relief-safricans.html

items.bewering: Soms word drade sonder toestemming van die verskaffer van elektrisiteit aan kraglyne gekoppel. So 'n draad noem ons 'n onwettige verbinding.
items.bron: Eskom, 'Electricity safety tips': a connection is illegal when it is made to the Eskom network without permission, 'for example by connecting to a mini-substation or overhead pole'. Sanews.gov.za, 'Eskom cautions against illegal connections'. https://www.eskom.co.za/?p=1330 ; https://www.sanews.gov.za/node/32666
items.regstelling: The lesson defines an illegal connection as a wire connected to power lines (kraglyne). Eskom names connections to a mini-substation (the green box in the street) as well as to an overhead pole. In a safety lesson this matters: a learner who sees a wire coming out of a mini-substation, which is not a kraglyn, will not recognise it from the lesson's definition, and the 'do not touch it' instruction is tied to 'so 'n draad'. Widen the definition to a connection to the electricity network without permission, for example to kraglyne or to a minisubstasie. The begrip entry carries the same narrowing (see below).

items.bewering: Sulke drade is dikwels onveilig gemaak en slordig neergelê. Party lê dwarsoor paadjies en ander plekke waar mense loop.
items.bron: Eskom, 'Electricity safety tips': illegal connections are usually unsafely built, and the wires often lie across pathways and walkways where passers-by can be electrocuted; Sanews: often lack insulation and are not hung at a safe height. https://www.eskom.co.za/?p=1330

items.bewering: So 'n draad kan iemand doodskok wat net daaraan raak, ook 'n kind wat niks daarmee te doen gehad het nie. Dit kan ook brande veroorsaak.

Sanews: eight-year-old electrocuted by a fence touching a live wire from an illegal connection. https://www.eskom.co.za/?p=1330 ; https://www.sanews.gov.za/index.ph%70/node/35423

items.bron: Eskom, 'Electricity safety tips': never touch low-hanging or carelessly laid cables; report illegal connections (0800 11 27 22); teach children about the danger. Telling an adult is the right route for a child. https://www.eskom.co.za/?p=1330

items.bewering: infrastruktuur: Al die geboue, masjiene, paaie en drade wat nodig is om dienste soos elektrisiteit te lewer.
items.bron: Matches the general meaning (the physical structures and facilities needed to deliver a service) and the Eskom chain above: mines, rail/road/conveyors, power stations, lines, substations. Read alone the entry is true. https://www.engineeringnews.co.za/article/eskom-sees-opportunity-for-emerging-coal-miners-to-improve-utilitys-security-of-supply-logistics-2018-02-01

items.bewering: substasie: 'n Plek met groot toestelle wat die elektrisiteit se stoot of pad verander.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Substation' and National Grid 'What is a substation': substations step voltage up or down with transformers and switch/route lines. 'Stoot' maps onto voltage (the standard 'push' picture) and 'pad' onto switching; both mappings hold. The word 'toestelle' here clashes with the lesson's own begrip for toestel, which is a separate item below. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substation ; https://nationalgrid.com/stories/energy-explained/what-is-a-substation

items.bewering: toestel: Iets wat die energie wat elektrisiteit bring, gebruik om lig, klank, beweging of hitte te gee. (Read together with substasie: 'n Plek met groot toestelle wat die elektrisiteit se stoot of pad verander.)
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Substation': a substation's equipment is transformers, circuit breakers, switches and busbars, which change voltage and route current. They do not use electricity to give light, sound, movement or heat. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substation
items.regstelling: Read alone, the toestel entry is a fair definition of an electrical appliance. But the substasie entry in the same lesson calls the equipment in a substation 'groot toestelle', and a learner who applies the lesson's own definition will conclude that this equipment gives light, sound, movement or heat. It does not: it changes the push (voltage) or the route. One of the two entries has to give. Simplest fix: call the substation equipment something the toestel definition does not cover (for example groot masjiene, which the lesson already uses for power-station equipment, or transformators). Do not widen the toestel definition, because the ketel/radio block depends on it meaning an appliance.

items.bron: US DOE lighting fact sheet: CFLs use 75% less energy for the same light; LEDs at least 75% (up to 90%) less. https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/ES-EE Lighting_080921.pdf

items.bewering: onwettige verbinding: 'n Draad wat sonder toestemming aan kraglyne gekoppel is.
items.bron: Eskom, 'Electricity safety tips': illegal = connected to the network without permission, for example to a mini-substation or an overhead pole. https://www.eskom.co.za/?p=1330
items.regstelling: A glossary entry is read alone, and this one limits an illegal connection to power lines. Widen it the same way as the study block, to a wire connected to the electricity network without permission, for example to kraglyne or to a minisubstasie, so a learner recognises a wire from a mini-substation as one too. Keep the entry and the block's opening sentence saying the same thing.

opsomming: The lesson is factually sound throughout (coal at 83% of SA electricity, heating loads highest, 90% of an old bulb's energy as heat, Eskom's illegal-connection dangers all confirmed), but two definitions need fixing: an illegal connection is defined as a wire to power lines only, while Eskom names mini-substations too, which matters in a safety block, and the substation entry calls its equipment 'toestelle' although the lesson's own toestel entry defines a toestel as something that gives light, sound, movement or heat.
